case_name: S. P. Shivprasad Pipal v Union of India and Others
facts: The appeal arises from a judgment and order of the central Administrative Tribunal at new Delhi dismissing the application filed by the appellant who was at the material time, labour Commissioner working in the Ministry of labour.
The Central Labour Service Rules, 1987 were brought into force by a notification dated 3.2.1987.

Under the notification of 3.2.1987 a Central Labour Service was created by merging the following three cadres: Central Industrial Relations Machinery, Labour officers (Central pool), and Labour Welfare Commissioners' cadre.

The appellant has challenged the constitution of a Central Labour Service under the Central Labour Service Rules, 1987, issued by the President in the exercise of powers conferred on him under the proviso to Art. 309 of the Constitution.
The merger of the three cadres was done after a detailed exercise and consideration of various factors.
issues: Whether the constitution of a Central Labour Service under the Central Labour Service Rules, 1987 is valid
Whether the merger of the three cadres is in violation of Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution
petitioner_arguments: The appellant has challenged the exercise of power under Art. 309 of the Constitution to formulate Central Labour Service Rules, 1987.
He has also challenged the merger of the three cadres on the ground that this is done in violation of Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution.
respondent_arguments: The respondents have stated that a detailed exercise was done to ensure that no injustice takes place to any of the merging cadres.

They have also stated that the question of merging of different cadres under the Ministry of Labour had been considered thrice in the past and every time the desirability of merging the cadres was invariably recommended.
court_reasoning: The principles which have to be borne in mind while considering the merger of different cadres are: In the matter of equation of posts, (1) where there were regularly constituted similar cadres in the different integrating units the cadres will ordinarily be integrated on that basis but (2) where there were no such similar cadres, the following factors will be taken into consideration in determining the equation of posts:-
The court further observed that it is not open to the court to consider whether the equation of posts made by the central Government is right or wrong.
This was a matter exclusively within the province of the Central Government.
holding: The Court held that the constitution of a Central Labour Service under the Central Labour Service Rules, 1987 is valid and the merger of the three cadres is not in violation of Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution.
The Court also observed that it is not open to the court to consider whether the equation of posts made by the central Government is right or wrong.
